segments.title: Chương 31: 0031
segments.content:
Monday.

Last night's "pillow talk" went on for so long that the entirety of Dorm 302 ended up sleeping in.

The stirring march from the broadcast speakers played on a loop, over and over again.

It wasn't until the last ten minutes or so that everyone, as if sleepwalking, got dressed and washed up, sprinting towards the main athletic field in a disheveled state.

Flag-raising ceremony!

After singing the national anthem, Wu Meng, a third-year senior, went on stage to give a speech, sharing methods for improving study efficiency.

During the speech, everyone took the opportunity to catch up on sleep.

That rascal Xie Yang fell asleep standing up, his body swaying back and forth without ever falling over.

Li Jun arrived late, carrying a backpack. His backpack was purely for show, specifically for carrying a basketball; there were usually no books inside.

It was a prestigious provincial key high school, yet its atmosphere was free and undisciplined.

For students like Li Jun who were late for the flag-raising ceremony, the school leaders and teachers turned a blind eye.

The third-year liberal arts stream had ten classes. In the past, Ou Yafei from Class 12 was the most eye-catching. Her looks and figure were already outstanding, and when paired with the ultimate weapon of makeup and styling, she became a beauty in a class of her own, standing out like a crane among chickens.

In 2003, high school girls in a small county town who knew how to apply makeup, and did it well, were few and far between!

Now, there was also Bian Guanyue.

A rivalry of beauties.

When the flag-raising ceremony was dismissed, many boys were secretly watching these two. They would often pretend to be chatting with friends, taking a few discreet glances as they walked before nonchalantly looking straight ahead again.

The boys often discussed in private who the real school belle was, Bian Guanyue or Ou Yafei.

Opinions varied, and there was no consensus.

But usually, Ou Yafei was more popular because she was so good at dressing up. She also had a lively and outgoing personality. If a boy she didn't know greeted her, Ou Yafei would always respond with a sweet smile.

Bian Guanyue was the exact opposite, cold and distant, pushing people away. She also never wore makeup, always showing her bare face.

Of course, some also said that Meng Jiayao from the science stream was very pretty and not much inferior to Bian Guanyue and Ou Yafei.

"Great Hero Chen, don't walk with us," Li Yulin pointed behind him. "Be careful, someone might steal Bian Guanyue away."

Chen Guiliang turned his head and saw that Zheng Feng was at it again, fawning over her.

What Bian Guanyue had said last night hadn't dispelled Zheng Feng's intentions at all.

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "Zheng Feng is wasting his time."

He had more or less figured out Bian Guanyue's personality.

Back in the classroom, before class started, Chen Guiliang took out his first-year math textbook to review.

High school at this time was really not as competitive as it would be more than ten years later.

At Chen Guiliang's school, they used the summer vacation between the second and third years to learn the third-year curriculum through remedial classes. The entire third-year curriculum wasn't finished until a week after the third-year midterm exams.

Starting this week, the teachers of each subject would begin reviewing the first and second-year material with the students.

Chen Guiliang was perfectly in sync with the teachers' pace.

While Chen Guiliang was studying math on his own, Bian Guanyue was memorizing English vocabulary. Her English was terrible, barely passing.

The morning passed by quickly.

At noon, after treating his roommates to a meal of mutton soup, Chen Guiliang came to the classroom for the afternoon self-study session and started working on the math practice worksheet the teacher had handed out.

After struggling for half an hour, Chen Guiliang's head was buzzing.

"You're here so early," Chen Guiliang greeted Bian Guanyue.

Bian Guanyue put down her backpack and said, "You're early too."

She had left home early at noon and taken the bus to school early, mainly to avoid Zheng Feng.

Bian Guanyue took out a few practice worksheets, glanced at Chen Guiliang's scratch paper, and asked curiously, "Are you writing a novel?"

Chen Guiliang explained, "I've been reviewing math for so long my head's all fuzzy. Writing a novel is a change of pace."

"Sci-fi?" Bian Guanyue saw a few keywords.

Chen Guiliang said, "Cyberpunk, within sci-fi. I submitted four pieces to the New Concept Writing Competition. One of them is called 'My Cyber Homeland,' and I plan to expand it into a full-length novel."

Bian Guanyue was confused. "I know what punk is, but what's cyberpunk?"

Chen Guiliang explained simply, "It's a type of dystopian science fiction novel that emerged twenty years ago. The plots usually involve hackers, artificial intelligence, and megacorporations."

Although Bian Guanyue didn't quite understand, her curiosity was piqued. "When you finish the novel, can you let me read it?"

"Of course, you'll be the first reader," Chen Guiliang readily agreed.

Traditional cyberpunk literature had come to an end in the late 80s and early 90s.

This was now the "post-cyberpunk era."

But in China, this genre wasn't even considered niche yet. That was because the vast majority of Chinese people had no concept of "cyberpunk" at all.

When people mentioned The Matrix, their first reaction was "sci-fi movie."

And that was it.

The full-length novel Chen Guiliang planned to write didn't have a virtual network world, but some of its ideas were very avant-garde.

"Avant-garde" here was in the context of 2003.

For example, the concept of "multitude" originated from "Empire," published in 2000. A more in-depth exploration, "Multitude: War and Democracy in the Age of Empire," had not even been published yet. This theory criticized the singularity of the traditional working class, emphasizing the joint resistance of diverse subjects in the context of globalization.

In Chen Guiliang's novel, the multitude was the main force resisting tyranny. In the early stages, they barely managed to form a popular front, but in the middle stages, they were divided and exploited by megacorporations, ultimately pushing the revolution towards anarchism.

There was also the "subaltern." In the novel's early revolutionary period, they were distorted and co-opted by megacorporations to be their dogs. The subaltern were essentially disadvantaged groups, but they were twisted into identity politics, with the LGBT community being the most typical example.

There were also social progress advocacy groups, which included the whole set of equal rights, animal protection, environmentalism, and humanitarianism. In the novel, all of these were distorted by megacorporations and turned into political tools for a pandemonium of freaks.

Chen Guiliang also included various metaphors in his novel.

For example, the "Memory Cleansing Program" of the megacorporation alliance in the book was a metaphor for the neoliberal "discourse reconstruction of the end of history theory," corresponding to how Europe and America in reality erased collective memories like the labor union movement and civil rights struggles.

Bian Guanyue worked seriously on her problems for half an hour, then turned her head to see Chen Guiliang still writing.

It was all novel settings.

Bian Guanyue couldn't help but ask, "There's a 'Diting' in a sci-fi novel?"

Chen Guiliang explained, "'Diting' is a voiceprint analysis matrix used by megacorporations to monitor civilians."

"Memories can be traded in the novel too?" Bian Guanyue asked, looking at the settings.

Chen Guiliang said:

"Every civilian, upon reaching adulthood, can choose to delete and replace their memories. This is because their childhood and adolescent experiences are unpleasant for them. They delete their original memories and sell them to those megacorporations. Then, the megacorporations re-instill a standard template of happy memories."

"If an adult's life becomes very painful, they can also sell these memories or choose to deposit them in a memory bank, and then pay to have custom happy memories instilled in them."

"Doing this accomplishes four things. One, you can make money. Two, you can be happy. Three, you can improve work efficiency. And four, you can maintain social stability."

"In the world of the novel, everyone enjoys endless happiness; pain is non-existent for them."

"Moreover, the laboring class can receive corporate welfare subsidies, having pleasure feedback systems implanted into their pain nerves free of charge. This way, the harder and more tired they are at work, the more pleasure they feel. Work-related injuries and such have all become blessings, and workers pride themselves on having more prosthetic limbs."

Bian Guanyue seriously considered such a society and couldn't help but exclaim, "That's terrifying!"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "As long as you can be happy, that's all that matters."

"After deleting painful memories, are you still your true self?" Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Yes and no. It depends on who you're facing."

"If you're facing family and friends, you can escape all responsibility by simply deleting and changing your memories, and you'll receive legal protection. For example, if someone abandons their wife and children, their memories have been deleted, so it's only natural that they wouldn't recognize their wife and children."

"But the law also stipulates that when deleting and replacing memories, basic corporate-related memories must be retained. No matter how the memories are changed, he is still a laborer for this corporation and must fulfill his labor obligations."

"So dark, so bizarre!" Bian Guanyue commented, then asked, "Are you planning to submit this to 'Mengya'? I'm afraid 'Mengya' readers won't like this kind of novel."

Chen Guiliang smiled.

"I don't have high hopes for it either. Its popularity definitely won't come close to 'Ice Fantasy,' but as long as a small group of people like it, that's enough. What you're looking at are the settings, which are rather dry. To attract more readers, the plot must be written in an interesting way. So, there has to be love."

"When the male protagonist makes his appearance, he has just come of age and is accompanied by his mother to have his memories deleted and replaced. He is very resistant to this because he likes a girl. Although the memory of his secret crush is painful, he still wants to keep it."

Bian Guanyue looked at the various settings on the paper, listened to Chen Guiliang's plot summary, and after a moment of contemplation, said, "I'm looking forward to this novel."

"Beep beep, beep beep!"

On the street outside the school, where there was no traffic jam, a Chery QQ honked from time to time.

Liu Shuying sat in the front passenger seat, saying helplessly to her husband, "Can you please stop showing off? What's there to show off about a car that costs thirty to forty thousand yuan?"

"There was a pedestrian on the road just now," Gao Zhan said.

Liu Shuying said, "Someone is walking on the side of the road, what does that have to do with you driving?"

Gao Zhan smiled. "I was afraid he might dart out."

The couple had always wanted to buy a car. When they found out the price of the Chery QQ in the summer, they immediately went to Rongcheng to place a preorder. The car was in such high demand that they had to wait a bitter four or five months for their turn. Last Saturday, they finally drove their new car home.

Now, Gao Zhan had to personally wash the car every day, rinsing it again and again, wiping it again and again. He was about to wipe the paint off the car.

Just as the couple drove the car onto campus, Liu Shuying's Bird mobile phone rang.

"Hello... Director Yang, hello. I just arrived at the school... Okay, okay, I'll be right over." Liu Shuying hung up the phone.

Gao Zhan had already parked the car and asked, "What's up?"

Liu Shuying said, "I don't know."

Gao Zhan said worriedly, "It's not Chen Guiliang causing trouble again, is it?"

"It's very likely." Liu Shuying was almost traumatized.

The most outrageous time, Chen Guiliang almost got into a fight with the security guard, and the couple was called back to the school at 11:30 at night to handle it.

It turned out that a student had gone out to buy a late-night snack, violating the school's dining ban at the time. The guard, treating a minor rule as a major decree, argued with the student, then shoved him repeatedly, snatched the food and threw it on the ground, and even cursed, insulting the student's mother.

Chen Guiliang didn't even know that student. He happened to run into the situation on his way back from buying laundry detergent outside the school and, surprisingly, stepped in to stand up for justice, arguing with the guard.

The student who broke the rule took the opportunity to run away, leaving only Chen Guiliang entangled with the guard. They pushed each other back and forth in a stalemate for several tens of minutes, and the guard had no choice but to call the homeroom teacher.

Liu Shuying was extremely speechless about this. When she was scolding Chen Guiliang, she was rendered speechless and amused by his replies.

Chen Guiliang stuck to his guns at the time: First, the guard shouldn't have started the physical altercation; second, the guard shouldn't have wasted food; third, the guard shouldn't have used profanity and insults; fourth, young people should speak up for justice.

How was one supposed to manage a student like this?

Liu Shuying had a massive headache!

"I'll go with you," Gao Zhan said.

The couple went to the Dean's Office together.

Dean of Instruction Yang Zhenzhong greeted them warmly and even personally poured them tea.

Seeing this scene, it didn't seem like a student had caused trouble. Liu Shuying immediately breathed a sigh of relief.

The three exchanged a few pleasantries, and Yang Zhenzhong invited them to sit down. "How is the newly transferred student, Bian Guanyue, doing?"

Liu Shuying skipped over Bian Guanyue's truancy and only said, "We'll have to wait for the monthly exam to know about her academic performance. But Bian Guanyue is very obedient, pays attention in class, and completes her homework well after class."

Yang Zhenzhong said, "Her father and I were classmates at the normal college, so I'm just asking casually. With his daughter transferring here alone, a father is bound to be worried."

Liu Shuying quickly said, "I will pay special attention to her studies."

"Her seat should also be changed. I heard she's still sitting in the last row," Yang Zhenzhong said. "Bian Guanyue's transfer fee was quite high, and her father might donate in the future to start a love and support student project."

Chen Guiliang was going to get a new deskmate again.

And junior Tao Xue, at this moment, was getting a PHS phone service.

This was a task her brother had given her: to buy a PHS phone for Chen Guiliang to make it easier to communicate about matters related to the private server.

Tao Xue planned to give "Senior Zhang Wei" a surprise.

The main consort has had too much screen time. It's time for the western consort to have her turn.
